title: Sell Mineral Rights in Deersville, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Deersville, OH | Harrison County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Deersville, Harrison County's Utica core? Learn how spacing units are laid out and what determines value, then get a cash offer.
heroLead: Deersville sits in eastern Harrison County, ground that's been divided into horizontal spacing units almost continuously since the Utica play's earliest years.
intro: Harrison County has more laid-out Utica spacing units than nearly any other county in Ohio, and Deersville-area farmland has been part of that development pattern for over a decade. If you own minerals here, understanding how these units actually work, and how your family's tract fits into one, helps make sense of what's on your royalty statement, if you're receiving one.
This is genuinely core ground, not flank acreage, which changes the baseline assumptions around what an offer typically looks like compared to counties further from the play's thickest rock.

sections.heading: How spacing units carve up farmland
paragraphs: A horizontal Utica well permit defines a specific unit boundary, often a mile or more long, that pulls together mineral interests from multiple adjoining tracts regardless of who owns each one individually. Everyone whose acreage falls inside that boundary gets pooled and paid proportionally, which is why your royalty statement lists a small decimal interest rather than a flat share of the well.
The Ohio Department of Natural Resources publishes permit and unit boundary data by township, which is the most direct way to check whether your Deersville-area tract falls inside a current unit.

sections.heading: What core-play density means for value
paragraphs: Because Harrison County has such extensive unit coverage already, a tract here is more likely to already be leased and pooled than in a less-developed county. If yours is producing, your division order and royalty statements are the clearest measure of value. If it's genuinely unleased, that's less common in this specific part of the county, and worth confirming carefully before assuming.

sections.heading: Confirming title through the county recorder
paragraphs: Harrison County deed records are held at the recorder's office in Cadiz. Because so much farmland around Deersville has stayed in the same families for generations, confirming your exact fractional share, especially if multiple heirs are involved, is usually the first real step before finalizing any offer.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my Deersville-area tract is inside a spacing unit?
faqs.answer: Check the Ohio Department of Natural Resources' well and permit database by township, or review your division order if the tract is already producing.

faqs.question: Is Deersville core or flank Utica ground?
faqs.answer: Core. Eastern Harrison County has seen extensive horizontal development since the earliest years of the play.

faqs.question: What if I'm not sure how many acres my family actually owns?
faqs.answer: A title search at the Harrison County Recorder's office will confirm your legal description and, combined with your fractional share, your net mineral acreage.
